correctness.rationale: Every nonnegative weighted sum of unordered cuts is realized by a weighted Boolean-coordinate embedding in L1; injectivity is exactly positive separation of each pair. Finite universality gives realization of every admissible vector, and ultrahomogeneity extends the label-wise diversity isomorphism exactly when the vectors agree, using uniqueness of the diversity cut decomposition. The rows of the pair-cut map are independent: twice each edge coordinate is the sum of its two endpoint singleton columns minus the column of the two-point cut (using the complementary representative if needed), with n=1 and n=2 immediate. Thus the fiber near a strictly positive vector is open relative to its translate of the kernel. The image of the positive orthant is nonempty and open by full row rank, and positive nullity at n=4 persists thereafter since successive differences are 2^(n−1)−n. The four-point perturbation adds one weight to each singleton cut and subtracts one from each two-plus-two cut; each pair sees net zero and the full-set value sees net one.
residual_risks: The affine dimension is for the full-diversity orbit coordinates at strictly positive weights, not a statement about automorphism orbits of the metric reduct or uniform dimension on boundary fibers. The finite rank calculation is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The result supplies a sharp observability threshold for a canonical homogeneous structure: labeled pair data suffice through three points but leave an explicit positive-dimensional continuum of inequivalent full configurations on an open set from four points onward. The exact arity dependence and the four-point perturbation are usable in distinguishing what the reduct does and does not retain; qualitative nonhomogeneity alone would not give these facts.
residual_risks: This is a bounded contribution about diversity-orbit information. It neither classifies boundary fibers nor resolves any orbit classification for the metric reduct itself.
